description_en: Located southwest of the Paśupati area, the Vanakālī Mandira is an open shrine situated within a jungle. The goddess, known as Vanakālī (meaning "Kālī of the forest"), is depicted as an eight-armed Kālī standing on a corpse, facing south. While most of the implements held in her hands are no longer identifiable, her top left hand holds a sacrificial sword (khaḍga), and the lower left hand grips a severed head by its locks. In her second right hand, she holds a small double-sided drum (ḍamaru) (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 473). One of her left hands can be seen devouring human flesh. Scholars such as Slusser (1982, plate 558) suggest that the statue dates back to the 9th-10th century, while Schroeder places its origin between the 9th and 12th centuries. Vanakālī also belongs to the group of Nine Goddesses of Paśupati Area (Michaels 1994, p. 91, and 2018, p. 43).There is no inscription specifically documenting the construction of the temple. According to chronicles, King Śivadevavarman caused the appearance of the Goddess Vanakālī, who had devoured an army during the reign of King Dharmadatta. She had retreated into the forest through a hidden path while cleansing the flesh stuck in her teeth (Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī2016, 12.133). Another later chronicle calledDevamālā Vaṃśāvalī(2013, p. 36) states that King Śivadeva established the Vanakālī statue in 388 CE (Kaligata Era 3489). However, no historical evidence supports the existence of a king named Śivadeva reigning around 388 CE in Nepal. On the other hand, D. Vajrācārya (VS 2030, pp. 366-367) published an undated Licchavi inscription found in the Vanakālī area, mentioning that King Aṃśuvarmā's wife established a deity, and Amṛtavarmā built a boundary wall around the temple premises. However, the inscription does not specifically mention the Vanakālī Mandira, as it was recovered from the Rājarājeśvarī Mandira area. Hence, it cannot be associated with the Vanakālī Mandira (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 584). The pedestal of the Vanakālī statue bears an inscription, but its content is unclear. It likely consists of a mantra related to the deity, and no date is mentioned. The script used in the inscription appears to belong to the later Licchavi period (Vajrācārya 1973, p. 131). Unfortunately, cleaning and photographing the inscription were not permitted. In 1958 CE (VS 2015), King Mahendra renovated the temple and erected a boundary wall around its premises.Local beliefs hold that worshiping Vanakālī helps remove obstacles hindering one's work and provides a cure for ailments that defy conventional remedies. The worship of Vanakālī is also believed to alleviate excessive crying in infants and toddlers.A Karmācārya priest performs daily rituals at the temple every morning. Annually, on the 3rd day of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha, a palanquin procession of Goddess Vanakālī takes place. The Paśupati Guṭhī Gośvārā, an institution responsible for various trusts in the Paśupati area, offers special worship to Vanakālī, accompanied by the sacrifice of a sheep twice a year, on the 14th day of the dark fortnight of Śrāvaṇa and the 14th day of the dark fortnight of Mārgaśīrṣa. Additionally, Vanakālī is honored during a special procession called Dīpaṅkhā Yātrā (Michaels 2013).In 1797 CE (VS 1854), King Raṇabahādura Śāha endowed 33ropanīsof land in Motīṭāra to establish a trust responsible for organizing the temple's anniversary rituals (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 585). Records from the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna indicate that 30ropanīsand one ānā of land are registered in the name of the trust associated with the Vanakālī Mandira (Guṭhī Saṃsthāna VS 2071, p. 32).
description_ne: लिच्छविकालीन अभिलेख कुँदिएको वनकालीदेवीको खटजात्रा प्रत्येक वर्ष वैशाख शुक्ल ३ मा मनाइन्छ ।पशुपति क्षेत्रको दक्षिण-पश्चिममा वनकालीको मन्दिर अवस्थित रहेको छ । वनमा रहेकी काली हुनाले यिनलाई वनकाली भनिएको हो । यसलाई मन्दिर भनिएपनि यहाँ कुनै मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको छैन । खुल्ला आकाशमुनि दक्षिणाभिमुख गरी देवस्थल बनाएर वनकालीदेवीको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । शवमाथि उभिएकी वनकालीका आठ हात छन् । हातका धेरै आयुधहरू खिइएर चिन्न नसकिने भइसकेका छन् । तिनमा बायाँ माथिल्लो हातमा खड्ग र तल्लो हातमा मुण्ड लिएको देखिन्छ भने दाहिनेपट्टिको दोस्रो हातमा डमरु छ (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.473) । बायाँ एउटा हातले मानिसको मासु खाइरहेको यस मूर्तिलाई Slusser (1982, plate 558) ले ईशाको ९-१० औं शताब्दीको अनुमान गरेकी छिन् भने Schroeder (2019, p.792, plate 248B) ले ९ औं - १२ औं शताब्दी बीचको अनुमान गरेका छन् ।वनकालीदेवीको स्थापनाबारे स्पष्ट रूपले अभिलेख लेखिएको पाइँदैन । वंशावलीअनुसार वनमा गुप्त रूपले बसिरहेकी यी देवीलाई सबैले देख्ने गरी प्रकाशमा ल्याइदिने काम राजा गुणकामदेवका छोरा राजा शिवदेववर्म्मनले गरेका थिए । राजा धर्मदत्तको पालामा युद्ध हुँदा सेनालाई मारेर खाएपछि दाँतमा अड्केको मासु औंलाले निकालिरहेको अवस्थाका वनकालीलाई राजा शिवदेववर्म्मनले ध्यान गरी देवीलाई प्रकाशमा ल्याइदिएका थिए (Nepālikabhūpavaṃśāvalī: 2016, 12.133) ।Devamālā Vaṃśāvalī(2013, p.36) मा कलिगत संवत् ३४८९ (सन् ३८८) मा राजा शिवदेवले वनकालीको मूर्ति प्रतिष्ठा गरी प्रख्यात गरिदिएको कुरा लेखिएको छ । सन् ३८८ तिर शिवदेव नाम गरेका राजाले शासन गरेको नभेटिने हुनाले वंशावलीमा लेखिएका यी कुरालाई प्रामाणिक मान्न सकिँदैन । D. Vajrācārya (VS 2030, pp.366-367) ले वनकालीमा रहेको मिति नभएको एउटा लिच्छवि अभिलेखको पाठ छापेका छन् । उक्त अभिलेखमा अंशुवर्माकी पत्नीले देवता स्थापना गरेको र अमृतवर्माले मन्दिरको इलाकालाई पर्खालले घेरेको भनी लेखिएको छ । तर सो अभिलेखमा वनकालीको नाम उल्लेख गरिएको छैन र अभिलेख वनकाली प्राङ्गणमा नभईकन राजराजेश्वरी मन्दिरको दक्षिणतर्फको पोखरीनजीक रहेकोले उक्त अभिलेखलाई वनकाली मन्दिरसँग सम्बन्धित गर्न मिल्दैन (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.584) । देवीको मूर्तिको पादपीठमा पनि अभिलेख कुँदिएको छ । उक्त अभिलेखमा मिति छैन र के लेखिएको भन्ने कुरा पनि बुझिँदैन, सम्भवत: कुनै मन्त्र लेखिएको हुनसक्छ । अभिलेखको लिपि हेर्दा पछिल्लो चरणको लिच्छवि लिपि देखिन्छ (Vajrācārya 1973, p.131) ।[1]विसं २०१५ (सन् १९५८) मा राजा महेन्द्रले मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरी पर्खाल लगाइदिएका थिए ।यी देवीको पूजा गरेमा रोकिएका काम सम्पन्न हुने, लामो समय औषधी उपचार गराउँदा पनि निको नभएको अवस्थामा यहाँ पूजा गरेपछि निको हुने विश्वास गरिन्छ । बच्चाहरू रुँदारुँदा सुक्दै जाने र अचेत हुन थालेमा यी देवीको पूजा गर्नाले निको हुने जनविश्वास छ । यस मन्दिरमा कर्माचार्यले पुजारीको रूपमा काम गरिरहेका छन् । उनले मन्दिरमा बिहान नित्यपूजा लगायत पर्वविशेषमा पूजा गर्छन् । कुलानन्द झाले बनाइदिएको बगैँचाबाट वनकालीको नित्यपूजाको लागि प्रतिदिन माला ल्याइन्थ्यो, तर बगैँचा मासिएपछि अहिले त्यो परम्परा बन्द भइसकेको छ (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.12) । प्रत्येक वर्ष वैशाख शुक्ल ३ (अक्षय तृतीया) का दिन वनकालीदेवीको खटजात्रा सञ्चालन गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण १४ (घण्टकर्ण चतुर्दशी) र मंसीर कृष्ण १४ (बाला चतुर्दशी) को दिनमा पशुपति गुठी गोश्वाराले विशेष पूजा पठाउने गर्छ । ती दिनहरूमा एक-एकवटा भेडा बलि दिइन्छ । दीपङ्खा यात्राको अवसरमा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका विभिन्न देवीदेवता पूजा गर्ने क्रममा वनकालीको पनि पूजा गरिन्छ ।राजा रणबहादुर शाहले विसं १८५४ (सन् १७९७) मा वनकालीको वर्षवर्द्धनपूजाका लागि मोतीटारको ३३ रोपनी जग्गा समर्पण गरी गुठी राखिदिएका थिए (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.585) । अहिले गुठी संस्थानको लगतअनुसार वनकाली गुठीको नाममा ३० रोपनी १ आना जग्गा रहेको छ (Guṭhī Saṃsthāna VS 2071, p.32) ।[1]अभिलेख सफा गर्न र नजीकबाट फोटो खिच्न दिइएन ।

historical_events.event_description: There is an undated inscription on the pedestal of the Vanakālī statue but the content is unclear. It probably is a mantra related to the deity.
King Raṇabahādura Śāha endowed 33ropanīs of land in Motīṭāra to set up a trust that observes the temple’s anniversary rituals.
King Mahendra renovated the temple and built walls around the temple premises.
Rāmaprasāda Ropākhetī and his wife Bebī Śarmā Ropākhetī offered a bell to the temple in memory of his parents Yadukumāra Śarmā and Ṭaṃkakumārī.

Rāmaprasāda Ropākhetī and his wife Bebī Śarmā Ropākhetī offered a certain item to the temple in memory of his parents Yadukumāra Śarmā and Ṭaṃkakumārī. The inscription does not mention the item offered.

historical_events.event_name: Installation of statues of Gaṇeśa and Bhairava
historical_events.event_description: Rāmaprasāda Ropākhetī and his wife Bebī Śarmā Ropākhetī established statues of Bhairava and Gaṇeśa at the temple premises in memory of his parents Yadukumāra Śarmā and Ṭaṃkakumārī. A fire ritual of 10 million oblations was also performed on the occasion.
Keśara Gaḍtaulā and Umā Gaḍtaulā offered three narrow oblong banners (patāḥ) to Goddess Vanakālī.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a patāḥ to Bhairava
historical_events.event_description: Together with sons Viveka and Rivāja, Rāmaprasāda Ropākhetī and his wife offered a narrow oblong banner (patāḥ) to Bhairava.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a patāḥ to Gaṇeśa
historical_events.event_description: Together with sons Viveka and Rivāja, Rāmaprasāda Ropākhetī and his wife offered a narrow oblong banner (patāḥ) to Gaṇeśa.
